source: REF·DB v1 plastics reference; E and CTE typical unfilled values at room temperature

polymers.name: Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene
polymers.app: Housings, enclosures, FDM prototypes, trim, tool handles.
good: Tough and impact resistant at room temperature
Easy to machine, glue (solvent weld) and paint
Cheap and universally stocked
Good dimensional stability for a commodity plastic
bad: Poor UV resistance: yellows and embrittles outdoors (use ASA)
Attacked by many solvents, esters and ketones
Not for structural or hot applications

polymers.name: Acrylonitrile styrene acrylate
polymers.app: Outdoor housings, antenna covers, external trim, UV-exposed prototypes.
good: Essentially ABS with genuine UV and weather resistance
Retains colour and impact strength outdoors
Machines and bonds like ABS

polymers.name: Polycarbonate
polymers.app: Machine guards, canopies, light covers, impact shields, sight windows.
good: Outstanding impact strength: effectively unbreakable in sheet
Transparent, and available flame-retardant
Good temperature range for a commodity polymer
Thermoformable
bad: Notch-sensitive: a sharp internal corner destroys its impact performance
Poor chemical resistance: cracks with many solvents and some threadlockers
Must be dried before moulding or it degrades

polymers.name: Poly(methyl methacrylate)
polymers.app: Windows, guards, light pipes, display panels, laser-cut fixtures.
good: Best optical clarity of the common plastics
Excellent UV and weather resistance
Laser cuts and polishes beautifully
Cheaper than PC
bad: Crazes badly under stress with solvents and some cleaners

polymers.name: Polypropylene
polymers.app: Chemical tanks, ducting, living hinges, labware, fluid handling.
good: Superb chemical resistance including acids and alkalis
Genuine fatigue resistance: the living-hinge polymer
Very low density (floats)
Low cost
bad: Almost impossible to bond: needs flame or plasma treatment
High thermal expansion; poor dimensional stability

polymers.name: High-density polyethylene
polymers.app: Tanks, chute liners, cutting boards, jig bases, chemical pipework.
good: Excellent chemical resistance
Very low friction and good wear resistance
Cheap and easy to machine
Weldable to itself
bad: Cannot be bonded with conventional adhesives

polymers.name: Ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene
polymers.app: Wear strips, chute and hopper liners, guide rails, low-friction pads.
good: Outstanding abrasion resistance: better than most metals
Very low coefficient of friction
Self-lubricating, quiet running
Good impact strength at low temperature
bad: Cannot be bonded or conventionally welded
Poor dimensional stability for precision parts

polymers.name: Polyoxymethylene (acetal)
polymers.app: Precision gears, bushes, rollers, jig components, valve parts, wear pads.
good: Best machinability of any thermoplastic: holds tight tolerances
Excellent dimensional stability and low moisture uptake
Good fatigue and wear resistance, low friction
Stiff and strong for its weight
bad: Very poor bonding: must be mechanically fastened
Attacked by strong acids and oxidising agents
POM-H can have centreline porosity in large sections: use POM-C for thick parts

polymers.name: Polyamide (nylon)
polymers.app: Gears, bushes, cable ties, guides, pulleys, fuel lines (PA11/12).
good: Tough and abrasion resistant
Good fatigue strength, quiet-running gears
Wide grade range including cast sections for large parts
Reasonable temperature capability
bad: Absorbs moisture: dimensions and properties drift significantly with humidity
That moisture uptake makes it poor for precision parts (use POM instead)
Grade differences matter: PA6 absorbs more than PA66; PA11/12 much less

polymers.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
polymers.app: Precision wear parts, bearing surfaces, bottles, films, insulation tapes.
good: Very good dimensional stability and low moisture uptake
Low friction with good wear resistance
Stiffer and harder than acetal
Good chemical resistance to dilute acids
bad: Hydrolyses in hot water and steam

polymers.name: Polybutylene terephthalate
polymers.app: Electrical connectors, switch bodies, housings, automotive electricals.
good: Excellent electrical properties, retained when wet
Good dimensional stability and fast moulding cycles
Better chemical resistance than PA
Good surface finish
bad: Hydrolyses at elevated temperature in water
Warps if gating and cooling aren't controlled

polymers.name: Polycarbonate-ABS blend
polymers.app: Tough equipment housings, instrument enclosures, automotive interiors.
good: Combines PC toughness with ABS processability
Better low-temperature impact than ABS
Good flame-retardant grades available
bad: Not for outdoor use without stabilisation
More expensive than either base polymer

polymers.name: Polyphenylene oxide / ether
polymers.app: Water-handling components, electrical housings, dimensionally critical parts.
good: Very low moisture absorption: outstanding dimensional stability
Excellent hydrolytic stability, good for hot water
Good electrical properties
Low density for an engineering polymer
bad: Poor resistance to hydrocarbons and chlorinated solvents

polymers.name: Polyvinyl chloride
polymers.app: Chemical pipework, ducting, tank linings, fume extraction, bund liners.
good: Excellent acid and alkali resistance
Inherently flame retardant
Very cheap; easy to solvent weld and fabricate
CPVC extends temperature to about 95 °C
bad: Low service temperature and poor impact when cold
Releases HCl if burned or overheated: machining and welding need extraction
Plasticised grades leach plasticiser over time

polymers.name: Polyphenylene sulphide
polymers.app: Pump components, hot fluid handling, chemically aggressive service, electrical parts at temperature.
good: Outstanding chemical resistance: no known solvent below 200 °C
Inherently flame retardant with low smoke
Excellent dimensional stability at temperature
Retains properties hot
bad: Brittle unfilled: almost always used glass or carbon filled

polymers.name: Polysulfone
polymers.app: Steam-sterilisable equipment, hot water fittings, medical and lab hardware.
good: Withstands repeated steam sterilisation
Good hydrolytic stability
Transparent amber; rigid and strong hot
Good electrical properties
bad: Poor resistance to ketones, esters and aromatics
Stress cracks readily in the presence of solvents

polymers.name: Polyphenylsulfone
polymers.app: Aircraft interior parts, sterilisable medical instruments, hot plumbing.
good: Best impact strength and toughness of the sulfones
Excellent hydrolytic stability: endless steam cycles
Good flame, smoke and toxicity performance for cabin use

polymers.name: Polyethersulfone
polymers.app: Hot water and steam service, membranes, electrical parts at temperature.
good: High continuous service temperature
Good creep resistance hot
Inherently flame retardant
Transparent grades available

polymers.name: Polyetherimide
polymers.app: Aircraft interior components, electrical insulators, sterilisable parts, high-temp fixtures.
good: Excellent flame, smoke and toxicity performance: a cabin-interior staple
High strength and stiffness retained hot
Good dimensional stability, low creep
Available as FDM filament for high-temp prototypes
bad: Attacked by chlorinated solvents and some paint strippers

polymers.name: Polyetheretherketone
polymers.app: Seals, back-up rings, bushes, insulators, valve seats, hot wear parts, cryogenic components.
good: Exceptional chemical resistance: very few attacking agents
Continuous service to about 250 °C, excellent creep resistance
Good wear and fatigue behaviour; works cryogenically too
Inherently low flammability and low outgassing
bad: Very expensive: design for minimum volume
Needs high processing temperatures and dry stock

polymers.name: Polyetherketoneketone
polymers.app: Additive-manufactured high-performance parts, composite matrices, aerospace brackets.
good: Similar capability to PEEK with better AM processability
Tuneable crystallinity for lower-warp printing
Excellent strength and chemical resistance
bad: Very expensive and less widely stocked than PEEK

polymers.name: Polyamide-imide
polymers.app: High-load bushings, thrust washers, seal rings, structural parts at temperature.
good: Highest strength and stiffness of any melt-processable polymer
Outstanding wear resistance under load and heat
Very low thermal expansion; excellent creep resistance
bad: Requires a long, costly post-cure cycle
Difficult to machine: slow and hard on tools

polymers.name: Polyimide
polymers.app: Hot bushings, seals, thermal isolators, vacuum and space hardware, flexible circuits (film).
good: Highest continuous temperature of the machinable polymers
Excellent in vacuum: very low outgassing
Self-lubricating grades for unlubricated hot bearings
Retains toughness cryogenically
bad: Astonishingly expensive: often priced per part, not per kg
Not melt-processable; parts are direct-formed then machined

polymers.name: Polybenzimidazole
polymers.app: Extreme-temperature bushings, insulators, seals, semiconductor handling.
good: Highest temperature capability of any commercial thermoplastic
Highest compressive strength of any polymer
Very low thermal expansion; excellent wear at temperature
bad: The most expensive common polymer by a wide margin
Extremely brittle and difficult to machine

polymers.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene
polymers.app: Seals, back-up rings, gaskets, low-friction faces, chemical linings, cryogenic seats.
good: Effectively universal chemical resistance
Lowest friction of any solid polymer
Very wide service range, cryogenic to 260 °C
Excellent electrical insulator, non-stick
bad: Creeps badly under load (cold flow): never a structural part
Very poor wear resistance unless filled (glass, carbon, bronze)
Cannot be melt-processed conventionally or bonded without etching
Produces hazardous fumes if overheated: control machining temperature and never smoke near swarf

polymers.name: Polyvinylidene fluoride
polymers.app: High-purity chemical pipework, pump bodies, valve components, semiconductor fluid handling.
good: Excellent chemical resistance with far better mechanical strength than PTFE
Weldable and machinable
Good UV resistance and abrasion resistance
High purity: low extractables
bad: Attacked by strong bases and some ketones
More expensive than PP or PVC
Piezoelectric grades behave oddly in high-vibration service

polymers.name: Perfluoroalkoxy / fluorinated ethylene propylene
polymers.app: High-purity tubing, linings, wire insulation, transparent chemical lines.
good: PTFE-class chemical resistance but genuinely melt-processable
Can be extruded, moulded and heat-sealed
Transparent: good for visible flow lines

polymers.name: Ethylene tetrafluoroethylene
polymers.app: Aerospace wire insulation, chemical liners, architectural film.
good: Much tougher and more cut-resistant than PTFE
Good chemical and radiation resistance
Lightweight for a fluoropolymer
Standard aerospace wire insulation
bad: Attacked by some amines and sulphonic acids

polymers.name: Polychlorotrifluoroethylene
polymers.app: Cryogenic valve seats, oxygen-service seals, low-permeation windows.
good: Lowest gas permeability of the fluoropolymers
Excellent cryogenic performance: a classic LOX-service material
Good dimensional stability, less cold flow than PTFE
bad: Harder and more brittle than PTFE

polymers.name: Thermoplastic polyurethane
polymers.app: Flexible seals, cable jackets, bellows, wheels, protective boots, printed flexible parts.
good: Outstanding abrasion and tear resistance
Wide hardness range from soft rubber to rigid
Good oil and grease resistance
Printable and mouldable
bad: Hydrolyses in hot humid conditions (polyester grades especially: use polyether)
Poor resistance to strong acids and bases

polymers.name: Ethylene propylene diene monomer
polymers.app: Phosphate-ester hydraulic seals, water and steam seals, weather seals, motor case insulation.
good: Excellent water, steam and weather resistance
The correct choice for phosphate-ester fluids (Skydrol) and brake fluid
Good electrical insulation
Wide temperature range
bad: Completely unsuitable for mineral oils and fuels: swells and dissolves

polymers.name: Nitrile / acrylonitrile butadiene rubber
polymers.app: Fuel and oil seals, o-rings, gaskets, hydraulic seals.
good: Excellent mineral oil, fuel and grease resistance
Cheap and universally available
Good abrasion and compression-set behaviour
Wide hardness range
bad: Poor ozone, UV and weather resistance: cracks in storage
Not for phosphate esters, ketones or strong acids
Hardens and takes a set when hot

polymers.name: Fluoroelastomer
polymers.app: Fuel system seals, hot oil seals, chemically aggressive o-rings, engine seals.
good: Wide chemical resistance with high-temperature capability
Excellent compression set at temperature
Very low gas permeability
Good ozone and weather resistance
bad: Not for phosphate esters, ketones, amines or hot water/steam
Poor low-temperature flexibility: check the cold end
Produces hazardous decomposition products if burned

polymers.name: Perfluoroelastomer
polymers.app: Ultimate chemical and temperature seals; semiconductor, aggressive process, critical aerospace.
good: Near-universal chemical resistance with elastomeric behaviour
Highest temperature elastomer available
Very low outgassing grades for vacuum

polymers.name: Silicone rubber
polymers.app: Extreme-temperature static seals, gaskets, thermal pads, medical and food contact.
good: Widest temperature range of the common elastomers, roughly −60 to +230 °C
Excellent ozone, UV and weather resistance
Physiologically inert; food and medical grades
Very low compression set hot
bad: Poor tear, abrasion and tensile strength: static duty only
Poor resistance to fuels, oils and steam
Silicone contamination ruins bonding and painting nearby: keep it away from bond shops

polymers.name: Polylactic acid
polymers.app: FDM prototypes, form models, checking fixtures, throwaway jigs.
good: Easiest material to 3D print: minimal warp
Stiff and dimensionally accurate when cold
Bio-derived, low odour
Cheap
bad: Softens around 55–60 °C: useless in a warm car or near a heater

polymers.name: Polyamide 12 (laser sintered)
polymers.app: Functional prototypes, ducting, brackets, complex one-off hardware.
good: Genuinely functional parts with isotropic-ish properties
Complex geometry with no tooling
Lower moisture uptake than PA6/PA66
Good chemical resistance
bad: Porous surface: needs sealing for fluid or vacuum service
Anisotropy and build-orientation effects still exist
Powder ageing changes properties batch to batch
